The Projection Method is a fundamental technique in computational fluid dynamics, originally developed by Jos Stam and others for stable fluid simulation.
It is a core component of the Stable Fluids method, which discretizes the Navier-Stokes equations on a fixed grid.

The method relies on the Helmholtz-Hodge decomposition theorem, which states that any vector field can be decomposed into a divergence-free component and a curl-free component (the gradient of a scalar potential, i.e., pressure).
